findings.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — P1, confidence 100: `String getShortcut();` adds an abstract method to the grant-provider SPI, so an already-deployed third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` has no implementation and `String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut();` at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 throws `AbstractMethodError` during provider initialization, preventing the server from booting with that extension.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — P2, confidence 100: `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)` hard-codes a two-character grant field while the factory contract says `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut`, so a conforming custom grant with a three-character shortcut emits a seven-character context through `grantShort + ':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()` and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` always rejects its own token ID instead of recovering its context.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — P2, confidence 100: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` validates `grantType` twice and admits a null raw token ID, so `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()` serializes it as the literal `null` and every such context for the same grant/session/token type receives the identical token ID, collapsing jti-based revocation and single-use identity.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — [P1][100] The rigid decoder check `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)` rejects every token minted by an extension grant using the documented “3-letters shortcut” from `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30`, so the new extensible grant-context framework cannot decode those access-token IDs.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — P1, confidence 100: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` reads the wrong two characters and rejects equality, so `isAccessTokenId` accepts UUID-suffixed access-token IDs with an incorrect grant shortcut and makes every updated event assertion falsely validate the new grant-context behavior.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — P1, confidence 100: `String getShortcut();` adds an abstract method to the grant-provider SPI, so an already-deployed third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` has no implementation and `String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut();` at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 throws `AbstractMethodError` during provider initialization, preventing the server from booting with that extension.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `String getShortcut();` is added as a new abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (line 33 in the interface file). This is a breaking change to an existing SPI. The `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` method iterates over all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on each one. Any third-party implementation of `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` that was compiled against the old interface version will not have this method implemented, causing an `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when `getShortcut()` is invoked. This is a real compatibility bug that would break existing extensions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — [P1][100] The rigid decoder check `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)` rejects every token minted by an extension grant using the documented “3-letters shortcut” from `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30`, so the new extensible grant-context framework cannot decode those access-token IDs.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that the 6-character length check rejects tokens from extension grants using '3-letters shortcut'. However, examining the diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() returns 2-character shortcuts (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'rt', 'ci', 'dg', 'pg', 'te', 'ro', 'pc'), not 3-letter shortcuts. The Javadoc comment says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but all actual implementations use 2 characters. The 6-character encoded context consists of: 2 chars for sessionType + 2 chars for tokenType + 2 chars for grantType = 6 chars total. This is consistent with the implementation. The finding misreads the documentation comment as a specification when the actual code uses 2-character shortcuts.
